newsitem.title: USA: Vermont says July revenues fell 4.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Vermont says July revenues fell 4.8 percent.

text.p: Vermont on Tuesday said its revenue collections in July fell 4.8 percent but it attributed the fall-off to some problems with collecting the data.

"The tax department began to fully utilize a computerized document scanner in July and there were some glitches," said Tom Pelham, the state Commissioner of Finance and Managment, in prepared remarks.

He estimated more than $3.5 million in personal income, sales and meals and rooms revenues received in July were not processed by the end of the month. "With the inclusion of these unprocessed revenues, July's revenues would have substantially met our expectations."

General Fund revenues totaled $51 million. While corporate income tax collections fell 47.5 percent to $800,000, the official said the drop could not be fully interpreted until September's quarterly payments were received.
Lottery and interest receipts each surpassed how much the state expected to get by $500,000, while the state got $865,000 more than it had anticipated from the estate tax.

Personal income tax collections added up to $21.7 million, down 6.1 percent, Sales and Use produced $16.8 million, down 3.1 percent, Rooms and Meals was $3.9 million, off 25 percent, Property Transfer came in at $1.2 million, down eight percent, and the All Other category contributed $6.6 million, up 30.1 percent.

For the Transportation Fund, July collections fell 13 percent to $8.8 million, a decline blamed on a processing backlag. Pelham said there was an 11-day backlog in revenue posting/categorization, which amounted to four days or $1.5 million more than usual for this period.
"As a result, we expect the Transportation Fund to make-up all of its lost receipts ground from July to August," the official said.

Gasoline taxes paid into the fund totaled $4.2 million, down 0.9 percent, Purchase and Use was $1.9 million, off 28.7 percent, Motor Vehicle Fees contributed $2.2 million, down 7.9 percent, and All Other produced $500,000, down 40.5 percent.
